1: # Agentic ODI 🚀
2: 
3: [![CI](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
4: 
5: > **Experimental test to learn and evaluate the feasibility of utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) specifications.**
6: 
7: ## 🌟 The Vision: Context-Aware Innovation
8: 
9: **Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)**, built on the "Jobs-to-be-Done" theory, relies on deeply understanding customer needs, desired outcomes, and execution contexts. Historically, applying ODI requires meticulous research, structured data modeling, and rigorous analysis.
10: 
11: **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** represents a paradigm shift in how AI systems consume and reason over external context. By adopting MCP, we can bridge the gap between static user research and dynamic, agentic AI. 
12: 
13: The vision for **Agentic ODI** is to build a unified, open protocol where LLMs and autonomous agents can natively query, understand, and reason over ODI data (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores) dynamically in real-time. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server will act as the "brain" of customer needs, allowing agents to invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions strictly anchored in verified user outcomes.
14: 
15: ## 🏗️ Current State (Experimental Testbed)
16: 
17: This repository serves as an initial sandbox for understanding server-client MCP communication streams. We are utilizing [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) to prototype HTTP-based context delivery.
18: 
19: ### Code Overview
20: 
21: This repository is a [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) made up of six installable packages, each with its own `pyproject.toml`, `src/` layout, and tests:
22: 
23: - **`core/`** (`agentic-odi-core`): Core domain models, repository abstractions, and the event-sourced IntentStore for Jobs, Steps, Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes with ODI opportunity-score computation.
24: - **`mcp_server/`** (`agentic-odi-mcp-server`): FastMCP-based MCP server exposing ODI tools and resources over HTTP. Hosts tools for Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes.
25: - **`local_server/`** (`agentic-odi-local-server`): Local, in-process adapter used by CLI to act as an MCP client while using the same repository layer.
26: - **`cli/`** (`agentic-odi-cli`): A [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based command-line interface. It provides a non-MCP entry point for interacting with Agentic ODI and also wraps the MCP server for certain operations.
27: - **`client/`** (`agentic-odi-client`): A Python-based agent client that communicates with the MCP server, executing tool calls over the active connection. It also hosts `run.py`, the local dev launcher that starts the server and the Streamlit UI together.
28: - **`connectors/`** (`agentic-odi-connectors`): Pluggable external integrations (ingest connectors). The first connector is an HTTP MCP **client** that can ingest resources from external MCP servers into the ODI store.
29: 
30: ## 🚀 Getting Started
31: 
32: ### Prerequisites
33: 
34: Python 3.10+ and [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). Install the whole workspace (all packages plus dev tooling):
35: 
36: ```bash
37: uv sync --all-packages
38: ```
39: 
40: This creates a `.venv` and installs `agentic-odi-core`, `agentic-odi-mcp-server`, `agentic-odi-local-server`, `agentic-odi-client`, `agentic-odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi-connectors` in editable mode.
41: 
42: ### Running the Environment
43: 
44: #### 🧰 Command-line interface (CLI)
45: 
46: Agentic ODI ships a [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based CLI so you can interact with the project directly from your terminal — no MCP client or chat UI required. Today it provides version/help plus commands for Customer Outcomes (`agentic-odi outcomes ...`) and external MCP connectors (`agentic-odi connectors ...`), giving you a scriptable, automation-friendly alternative to the MCP/chat path.
47: 
48: Launch it with:
49: 
50: ```bash
51: python -m cli --version   # print the Agentic ODI version
52: python -m cli --help      # show available options and commands
53: python -m cli             # show help when no command is given
54: ```
55: 
56: A console script is also installed, so `agentic-odi --version` works the same way.
57: 
58: #### Manage Customer Outcomes
59: 
60: Manage Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value) via the CLI. The CLI acts as an MCP client, so the server must be running (`python -m mcp_server`):
61: 
62: ```bash
63: # Add a Customer Outcome
64: agentic-odi outcomes add --job-id <job-id>   --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors"   --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding"   --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2   --category cost_reduction   --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn"
65: 
66: # List outcomes (optionally filtered)
67: agentic-odi outcomes list
68: agentic-odi outcomes list --job-id <job-id>
69: 
70: # Get, update, delete
71: agentic-odi outcomes get <outcome-id>
72: agentic-odi outcomes update <outcome-id> --importance 9.0
73: agentic-odi outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes
74: 
75: # Compute ODI Opportunity Score
76: agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2
77: ```
78: 
79: Set `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` to point to a non-default server if needed.
80: 
81: ### External connectors (MCP ingest)
82: 
83: The `connectors/` package enables ingesting external resources via MCP. Configure connectors via `--config` (default: `.agentic-odi/connectors.json`).
84: 
85: ```bash
86: # List configured connectors
87: agentic-odi connectors list
88: agentic-odi connectors list --config /path/to/connectors.json
89: 
90: # Add an HTTP MCP connector
91: agentic-odi connectors add mcp --name my-connector --url http://localhost:9000/mcp
92: 
93: # Check connector health
94: agentic-odi connectors health --name my-connector
95: 
96: # Ingest resources from the connector into the local store (idempotent by URI)
97: agentic-odi connectors ingest --name my-connector
98: ```
99: 
100: 
101: 
102: #### ⚡ One-command launch (recommended)
103: 
104: `python -m client.run` starts both the MCP server and the Streamlit UI concurrently. Press **Ctrl+C** to stop both.
105: 
106: ```bash
107: python -m client.run
108: ```
109: 
110: | Service | URL |
111: |---|---|
112: | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp |
113: | Streamlit Chat UI | http://localhost:8501 |
114: 
115: #### 🔧 Manual split-terminal (alternative)
116: 
117: Open two terminals and run each process separately:
118: 
119: ```bash
120: # Terminal 1 — MCP server
121: python -m mcp_server
122: 
123: # Terminal 2 — Streamlit chat UI
124: streamlit run client/src/client/app.py
125: ```
126: 
127: ### Local tools-capable LLM backend (for MCP testing)
128: 
129: To exercise real tool-calling end-to-end against the MCP server, you need a local LLM backend that:
130: 
131: - Exposes an **OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API** (for example, `/v1/chat/completions`), and
132: - Supports OpenAI-style **`tools` / `tool_calls`**.
133: 
134: A simple fully local option is [`llama-cpp-python`](https://github.com/abetlen/llama-cpp-python), which can run a quantized model on your machine and expose an OpenAI-compatible server.
135: 
136: 1. **Install a local LLM server**
137: 
138:    Install `llama-cpp-python` in your environment (see its README for platform-specific build notes):
139: 
140:    ```bash
141:    pip install llama-cpp-python
142:    ```
143: 
144: 2. **Download a small tools-capable model**
145: 
146:    Download a small GGUF model that supports function/tool calling (for example, a 7B function-calling variant from Hugging Face) and note its path, e.g. `C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf`.
147: 
148: 3. **Start the OpenAI-compatible server**
149: 
150:    Start the server and give the model a friendly alias that matches the default used by the Streamlit client (`client/src/client/app.py`):
151: 
152:    ```bash
153:    python -m llama_cpp.server \
154:      --model "C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf" \
155:      --model_alias local-tools-model \
156:      --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 \
157:      --chat_format openai
158:    ```
159: 
160:    This exposes an OpenAI-style API at `http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1`.
161: 
162: 4. **Point the Streamlit client at the local server**
163: 
164:    `client/src/client/app.py` reads defaults from environment variables (with sensible fallbacks):
165: 
166:    - `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` (default: `http://localhost:8001/v1`)
167:    - `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` (default: `local`)
168:    - `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` (default: `local-tools-model`)
169:    - `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` (default: `http://localhost:8000/mcp`)
170: 
171:    You can either set these in your shell or adjust them in the Streamlit sidebar under **“LLM Configuration”**.
172: 
173: 5. **Verify tool-calling against the MCP server**
174: 
175:    - (Optional) Before starting the UI, you can quickly verify that the LLM backend is reachable:
176: 
177:      ```bash
178:      curl http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/models
179:      ```
180: 
181:      If this request fails, fix your local LLM server configuration before debugging the MCP client/server.
182: 
183:    - Start the MCP server and Streamlit UI (either via `python -m client.run` or the split-terminal commands above).
184:    - In the browser UI, ask the assistant something that should use ODI tools, for example: “Help me define a new Job-to-be-Done and add it to your ODI repository.”
185:    - You should see the assistant briefly display that it is calling tools (for example, `add_job`, `get_jobs`, etc.) and then respond with grounded ODI guidance, confirming that the local LLM, MCP server, and client wiring all work together.
186:    - If the LLM backend is unreachable or misconfigured, the UI will show a clear error banner indicating that the backend at your configured **Base URL** could not be reached, along with details from the underlying error. Use that message together with the steps above to fix your local LLM setup.
187: 
188: #### 🤖 Agent-driven testing
189: 
190: Type `/dev` in the AI assistant to trigger the full automated workflow: it will start both processes, open the browser, send a test message, and report the results.
191: 
192: ## 🧪 Testing
193: 
194: Tests use **pytest** with **pytest-asyncio** (strict mode) and run entirely in-memory — no running server required. Each project owns its tests. CI runs the suite on Python **3.10, 3.11, and 3.12** and stores a coverage report as a build artifact:
195: 
196: ```bash
197: uv run --directory core pytest
198: uv run --directory mcp_server pytest
199: uv run --directory local_server pytest
200: uv run --directory client pytest
201: uv run --directory cli pytest
202: uv run --directory connectors pytest
203: ```
204: 
205: ### 🧠 Agent session tracking
206: 
207: Agent sessions are captured with the [Entire](https://docs.entire.io/overview) CLI. The repository integration lives in `.entire/settings.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, and `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`. Run `entire status` to confirm it is enabled and `entire checkpoint list` to inspect captured checkpoints.
208: 
209: ### 🧹 Linting, formatting & type checks (CI parity)
210: 
211: The CI pipeline runs several quality checks. You can mirror them locally with:
212: 
213: ```bash
214: # Ruff lint and formatting checks (per-file config comes from each project's pyproject.toml)
215: uv run ruff check .
216: uv run ruff format --check .
217: 
218: # Type checking (run per project so each project's config applies)
219: uv run --directory core mypy .
220: uv run --directory mcp_server mypy .
221: uv run --directory local_server mypy .
222: uv run --directory client mypy .
223: uv run --directory cli mypy .
224: uv run --directory connectors mypy .
225: 
226: # Security scanning
227: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r cli/src client/src core/src local_server/src mcp_server/src connectors/src
228: 
229: # Tests (same as CI)
230: uv run --directory core pytest
231: uv run --directory mcp_server pytest
232: uv run --directory local_server pytest
233: uv run --directory client pytest
234: uv run --directory cli pytest
235: uv run --directory connectors pytest
236: ```
237: 
238: To run these automatically before each commit, you can enable the bundled pre-commit hooks:
239: 
240: ```bash
241: uv tool install pre-commit
242: pre-commit install
243: ```
244: 
245: After this, `ruff` and `ruff-format` will run on staged files whenever you commit. You can also trigger them manually with:
246: 
247: ```bash
248: pre-commit run --all-files

# Agentic ODI 🚀

[![CI](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

> **Experimental test to learn and evaluate the feasibility of utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) specifications.**

## 🌟 The Vision: Context-Aware Innovation

**Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)**, built on the "Jobs-to-be-Done" theory, relies on deeply understanding customer needs, desired outcomes, and execution contexts. Historically, applying ODI requires meticulous research, structured data modeling, and rigorous analysis.

**Model Context Protocol (MCP)** represents a paradigm shift in how AI systems consume and reason over external context. By adopting MCP, we can bridge the gap between static user research and dynamic, agentic AI. 

The vision for **Agentic ODI** is to build a unified, open protocol where LLMs and autonomous agents can natively query, understand, and reason over ODI data (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores) dynamically in real-time. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server will act as the "brain" of customer needs, allowing agents to invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions strictly anchored in verified user outcomes.

## 🏗️ Current State (Experimental Testbed)

This repository serves as an initial sandbox for understanding server-client MCP communication streams. We are utilizing [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) to prototype HTTP-based context delivery.

### Code Overview

display.text:
# Agentic ODI 🚀

[![CI](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

> **Experimental test to learn and evaluate the feasibility of utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) specifications.**

## 🌟 The Vision: Context-Aware Innovation

**Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)**, built on the "Jobs-to-be-Done" theory, relies on deeply understanding customer needs, desired outcomes, and execution contexts. Historically, applying ODI requires meticulous research, structured data modeling, and rigorous analysis.

**Model Context Protocol (MCP)** represents a paradigm shift in how AI systems consume and reason over external context. By adopting MCP, we can bridge the gap between static user research and dynamic, agentic AI. 

The vision for **Agentic ODI** is to build a unified, open protocol where LLMs and autonomous agents can natively query, understand, and reason over ODI data (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores) dynamically in real-time. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server will act as the "brain" of customer needs, allowing agents to invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions strictly anchored in verified user outcomes.

## 🏗️ Current State (Experimental Testbed)

This repository serves as an initial sandbox for understanding server-client MCP communication streams. We are utilizing [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) to prototype HTTP-based context delivery.

### Code Overview

This repository is a [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) made up of six installable packages, each with its own `pyproject.toml`, `src/` layout, and tests:

- **`core/`** (`agentic-odi-core`): Core domain models, repository abstractions, and the event-sourced IntentStore for Jobs, Steps, Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes with ODI opportunity-score computation.
- **`mcp_server/`** (`agentic-odi-mcp-server`): FastMCP-based MCP server exposing ODI tools and resources over HTTP. Hosts tools for Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes.
- **`local_server/`** (`agentic-odi-local-server`): Local, in-process adapter used by CLI to act as an MCP client while using the same repository layer.
- **`cli/`** (`agentic-odi-cli`): A [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based command-line interface. It provides a non-MCP entry point for interacting with Agentic ODI and also wraps the MCP server for certain operations.
- **`client/`** (`agentic-odi-client`): A Python-based agent client that communicates with the MCP server, executing tool calls over the active connection. It also hosts `run.py`, the local dev launcher that starts the server and the Streamlit UI together.
- **`connectors/`** (`agentic-odi-connectors`): Pluggable external integrations (ingest connectors). The first connector is an HTTP MCP **client** that can ingest resources from external MCP servers into the ODI store.

## 🚀 Getting Started

### Prerequisites

Python 3.10+ and [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). Install the whole workspace (all packages plus dev tooling):

```bash
uv sync --all-packages
```

This creates a `.venv` and installs `agentic-odi-core`, `agentic-odi-mcp-server`, `agentic-odi-local-server`, `agentic-odi-client`, `agentic-odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi-connectors` in editable mode.

### Running the Environment

#### 🧰 Command-line interface (CLI)

Agentic ODI ships a [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based CLI so you can interact with the project directly from your terminal — no MCP client or chat UI required. Today it provides version/help plus commands for Customer Outcomes (`agentic-odi outcomes ...`) and external MCP connectors (`agentic-odi connectors ...`), giving you a scriptable, automation-friendly alternative to the MCP/chat path.

Launch it with:

```bash
python -m cli --version   # print the Agentic ODI version
python -m cli --help      # show available options and commands
python -m cli             # show help when no command is given
```

A console script is also installed, so `agentic-odi --version` works the same way.

#### Manage Customer Outcomes

Manage Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value) via the CLI. The CLI acts as an MCP client, so the server must be running (`python -m mcp_server`):

```bash
# Add a Customer Outcome
agentic-odi outcomes add --job-id <job-id>   --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors"   --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding"   --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2   --category cost_reduction   --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn"

# List outcomes (optionally filtered)
agentic-odi outcomes list
agentic-odi outcomes list --job-id <job-id>

# Get, update, delete
agentic-odi outcomes get <outcome-id>
agentic-odi outcomes update <outcome-id> --importance 9.0
agentic-odi outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes

# Compute ODI Opportunity Score
agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2
```

Set `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` to point to a non-default server if needed.

### External connectors (MCP ingest)

The `connectors/` package enables ingesting external resources via MCP. Configure connectors via `--config` (default: `.agentic-odi/connectors.json`).

```bash
# List configured connectors
agentic-odi connectors list
agentic-odi connectors list --config /path/to/connectors.json

# Add an HTTP MCP connector
agentic-odi connectors add mcp --name my-connector --url http://localhost:9000/mcp

# Check connector health
agentic-odi connectors health --name my-connector

# Ingest resources from the connector into the local store (idempotent by URI)
agentic-odi connectors ingest --name my-connector
```



#### ⚡ One-command launch (recommended)

`python -m client.run` starts both the MCP server and the Streamlit UI concurrently. Press **Ctrl+C** to stop both.

```bash
python -m client.run
```

| Service | URL |
|---|---|
| MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp |
| Streamlit Chat UI | http://localhost:8501 |

#### 🔧 Manual split-terminal (alternative)

Open two terminals and run each process separately:

```bash
# Terminal 1 — MCP server
python -m mcp_server

# Terminal 2 — Streamlit chat UI
streamlit run client/src/client/app.py
```

### Local tools-capable LLM backend (for MCP testing)

To exercise real tool-calling end-to-end against the MCP server, you need a local LLM backend that:

- Exposes an **OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API** (for example, `/v1/chat/completions`), and
- Supports OpenAI-style **`tools` / `tool_calls`**.

A simple fully local option is [`llama-cpp-python`](https://github.com/abetlen/llama-cpp-python), which can run a quantized model on your machine and expose an OpenAI-compatible server.

1. **Install a local LLM server**

   Install `llama-cpp-python` in your environment (see its README for platform-specific build notes):

   ```bash
   pip install llama-cpp-python
   ```

2. **Download a small tools-capable model**

   Download a small GGUF model that supports function/tool calling (for example, a 7B function-calling variant from Hugging Face) and note its path, e.g. `C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf`.

3. **Start the OpenAI-compatible server**

   Start the server and give the model a friendly alias that matches the default used by the Streamlit client (`client/src/client/app.py`):

   ```bash
   python -m llama_cpp.server \
     --model "C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf" \
     --model_alias local-tools-model \
     --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 \
     --chat_format openai
   ```

   This exposes an OpenAI-style API at `http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1`.

4. **Point the Streamlit client at the local server**

   `client/src/client/app.py` reads defaults from environment variables (with sensible fallbacks):

   - `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` (default: `http://localhost:8001/v1`)
   - `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` (default: `local`)
   - `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` (default: `local-tools-model`)
   - `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` (default: `http://localhost:8000/mcp`)

   You can either set these in your shell or adjust them in the Streamlit sidebar under **“LLM Configuration”**.

5. **Verify tool-calling against the MCP server**

   - (Optional) Before starting the UI, you can quickly verify that the LLM backend is reachable:

     ```bash
     curl http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/models
     ```

     If this request fails, fix your local LLM server configuration before debugging the MCP client/server.

   - Start the MCP server and Streamlit UI (either via `python -m client.run` or the split-terminal commands above).
   - In the browser UI, ask the assistant something that should use ODI tools, for example: “Help me define a new Job-to-be-Done and add it to your ODI repository.”
   - You should see the assistant briefly display that it is calling tools (for example, `add_job`, `get_jobs`, etc.) and then respond with grounded ODI guidance, confirming that the local LLM, MCP server, and client wiring all work together.
   - If the LLM backend is unreachable or misconfigured, the UI will show a clear error banner indicating that the backend at your configured **Base URL** could not be reached, along with details from the underlying error. Use that message together with the steps above to fix your local LLM setup.

#### 🤖 Agent-driven testing

Type `/dev` in the AI assistant to trigger the full automated workflow: it will start both processes, open the browser, send a test message, and report the results.

## 🧪 Testing

Tests use **pytest** with **pytest-asyncio** (strict mode) and run entirely in-memory — no running server required. Each project owns its tests. CI runs the suite on Python **3.10, 3.11, and 3.12** and stores a coverage report as a build artifact:

```bash
uv run --directory core pytest
uv run --directory mcp_server pytest
uv run --directory local_server pytest
uv run --directory client pytest
uv run --directory cli pytest
uv run --directory connectors pytest
```

### 🧠 Agent session tracking

Agent sessions are captured with the [Entire](https://docs.entire.io/overview) CLI. The repository integration lives in `.entire/settings.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, and `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`. Run `entire status` to confirm it is enabled and `entire checkpoint list` to inspect captured checkpoints.

### 🧹 Linting, formatting & type checks (CI parity)

The CI pipeline runs several quality checks. You can mirror them locally with:

```bash
# Ruff lint and formatting checks (per-file config comes from each project's pyproject.toml)
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .

# Type checking (run per project so each project's config applies)
uv run --directory core mypy .
uv run --directory mcp_server mypy .
uv run --directory local_server mypy .
uv run --directory client mypy .
uv run --directory cli mypy .
uv run --directory connectors mypy .

# Security scanning
uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r cli/src client/src core/src local_server/src mcp_server/src connectors/src

# Tests (same as CI)
uv run --directory core pytest
uv run --directory mcp_server pytest
uv run --directory local_server pytest
uv run --directory client pytest
uv run --directory cli pytest
uv run --directory connectors pytest
```

To run these automatically before each commit, you can enable the bundled pre-commit hooks:

```bash
uv tool install pre-commit
pre-commit install
```

After this, `ruff` and `ruff-format` will run on staged files whenever you commit. You can also trigger them manually with:

```bash
pre-commit run --all-files
```

### 🧼 Developer workflow for formatting

- **When editing Python files**, either:
  - Rely on the **pre-commit hooks** above (recommended), or
  - Run Ruff formatting directly before pushing:

    ```bash
    uv run ruff format .
    ```

- **CI behavior**:
  - CI runs `uv run ruff check .` to lint without modifying files.
  - CI runs `uv run ruff format --check .` to *verify* formatting only.
  - If CI fails on formatting, run `uv run ruff format .` locally, commit the changes, and push again.

| File | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `mcp_server/tests/test_odi.py` | Full ODI workflow (add job → steps → outcomes → retrieval) + capabilities tool |
| `mcp_server/tests/test_customer_outcomes.py` | Customer Outcomes CRUD, filtering, computed opportunity scores, and tool validation |
| `mcp_server/tests/test_server_tools.py` | Error handling and retrieval for the MCP tools |
| `mcp_server/tests/test_tools.py` | Tool response-shape contract for `add_job` |
| `client/tests/test_run.py` | Dev launcher helpers (port checks) |
| `cli/tests/test_cli.py` | CLI `--version` and `--help` behavior |
| `cli/tests/test_outcomes_cli.py` | Customer Outcomes CLI subcommands with MCP stub |
| `cli/tests/test_connectors_cli.py` | `connectors` CLI subcommands (`list`, `add mcp`, `health`, `ingest`) with a stubbed client factory |
| `connectors/tests/test_models.py` | `ConnectorConfig` validation and MCP settings parsing |
| `connectors/tests/test_registry.py` | JSON registry load/save, duplicate/missing handling, malformed file errors |
| `connectors/tests/test_sink.py` | `IngestSink` append/batches/dump and idempotency by URI |
| `connectors/tests/test_mcp_connector.py` | `MCPClientConnector` against an in-memory `fastmcp.Client(server)` (health, catalog, ingest) |

**Conventions:**
- Test files live under each project's `tests/` directory and are named `test_*.py`.
- Every async test is decorated with `@pytest.mark.asyncio`.
- Use `Client(mcp)` directly (no HTTP server needed) for fast, isolated tests.
- The server's `reset_db` autouse fixture clears in-memory state before each test.

> [!TIP]
> Type `/test` in the AI assistant to have the agent run all tests and report the results automatically.

## ☁️ Deployment

The server is deployed via **[Horizon Prefect](https://www.prefect.io/horizon)**, Prefect's managed infrastructure for hosting MCP-compatible agents.

### 🧪 Test Chat (UI)

Interact with the deployed agent directly in your browser:

> **[https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat](https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat)**

### 🔌 MCP Server Endpoint

Integrate via the MCP protocol at:

> **[https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp](https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp)**

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Authentication is required** to access the MCP server endpoint. Please reach out to the maintainers to obtain the necessary credentials before connecting a client.

---

## 🗺️ Roadmap & Next Steps

As we validate the feasibility of this architecture, our next milestones include:

- [ ] **ODI Schema Definition**: Define standardized Pydantic models for *Jobs*, *Steps*, and *Outcomes*.
- [x] **CLI Dataset Commands**: Extend `cli/` so the ODI dataset can be created, queried, and scored from the terminal, in addition to the current MCP path.
- [x] **Generic Integrations (External Data Connectors)**: Pluggable `connectors/` package with an HTTP MCP **client** connector (`agentic-odi connectors list|add mcp|health|ingest`); more kinds to follow.
- [ ] **Context Tooling**: Replace the dummy `greet` tool with capabilities like `get_job_map(job_id)` or `evaluate_outcome(statement)`.
- [ ] **Data Persistence Layer**: Connect the fastmcp server to a lightweight vector or relational database containing actual user research data.
- [ ] **Agentic Integration**: Hook the client up to an LLM (e.g., via LangChain or standard OpenAI clients) so the LLM can *discover* the ODI tools and intelligently request customer insights when ideating features.

---
